Most AI governance courses look mainly at the US–China race. This module goes further. It looks at what the US and China want, how each sees the world, and where **middle powers like the EU and the Netherlands** fit in between. For every topic, you go to the **primary sources**: laws, official strategies, and documents from governments and AI labs, so you can check things for yourself.

You don't need a technical or legal background.

## How to use this module

1. **Go week by week.** Each week builds on the one before: why governance matters → who the players are → what policymakers act on → how Europe answered.
2. **Start with the ⭐ core readings.** They take about an hour a week. Everything else is optional depth.
3. **Join or recreate the discussion.** Every week has a [discussion session](discussions.qmd) with questions and an extra academic reading.
4. **Finish with the [final essay](essay.qmd):** a short research proposal on an open question in EU/NL AI governance.

## Workload

| Activity | Time per week |
|---|---|
| Lecture (or self-study of the week page) | 1.5 h |
| Core readings | ~1 h |
| Project / essay work | 1–2 h |
| Discussion group (optional, recommended) | 1.5 h |

## Every link has a backup

Each reading links to its **original source**. Next to it is an **archived copy** on the [Internet Archive](https://web.archive.org/), so the module keeps working if a page moves or disappears. See [About & sources](about.qmd).

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
This module follows the first run of the **SAIN Utrecht AI Governance course** (November–December 2026). It's an independent study guide, not an official SAIN publication. For live sessions, see [SAIN Utrecht events](https://luma.com/sain-utrecht-events).
:::
